messages:
sophia (Docs): Heads up — I'm drafting release notes for the 0.9.0 runtime rollout. Need concise callouts: batching improvements, KV-cache prefix caching, and the default quantization change. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4578 — can folks skim for accuracy + known issues?

kevin: On it. I'll scan the SDK snippets (python + ts). Any explicit migration steps we should show for customers currently pinned to the old quantization behavior?

sophia (Docs): Yes — add a tiny migration example for the CLI and a note about pinning model variants. Example CLI snippet (inline):

```
redwood model set-variant --model my-chat --variant v0.9 --quant none
```

marta (PM): Please also include a short known-issue callout: "embeddings recalibration for >32k contexts may regress similarity scores" with a one-line workaround (shorter rolling window + post-rerank).

noah: I found a stale anchor in the SDK page (/docs/sdk#old-streams) that 301s -> /docs/sdk/streams — I'll fix the link and add a redirect note in the changelog entry.

kevin: Quick ask: @sophia, want a 4–6 line Python streaming example that uses the new streaming API? I'll add a small code block that fits the docs layout.

sophia (Docs): Yes please, keep it compact and show how to attach to the KV cache header. Tone should be technical, not marketing.

kevin: Pushing commit in ~10m, snippet preview: 
```
from redwood import Client
c = Client()
for token in c.chat.stream(model="kestrel-v0.9", prompt="hi"):
    print(token.text, end="")
```

marta (PM): Also sanity-check the Dedicated SLA phrasing — don't promise <50ms p95 unless it's behind Dedicated capacity. I'll add SLA numbers in a follow-up commit.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Link-check started on branch relnotes-0.9.0 — scanning 12 files.

noah: Link-check flagged one redirect and a missing image alt on the kernel-ops doc. I'll open a small PR for the image alt + redirect.

sophia (Docs): Great. Plan: freeze copy by EOD so we can publish the relnotes tomorrow morning. If anything reads too "marketing-ey", please mark with :scissors: and change to product/technical wording. Thanks all! :tada:
